source_text: Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος ἀπεφήνατο λέγων· Οἱ μὴ βουληθέντες θῦσαι τοῖς θεοῖς, καὶ εἶξαι τῷ τοῦ αὐτοκράτορος προστάγματι, μαστιγωθέντες ἀπαχθήτωσαν κεφαλικὴν ἀποτιννύντες δίκην κατὰ τὴν τῶν νόμων ἀκολουθίαν. Οἱ ἅγιοι μάρτυρες δοξάζοντες τὸν Θεὸν, ἐξελθόντες ἐπὶ τὸν συνήθη τόπον, ἀπετμήθησαν τὰς κεφαλὰς, καὶ ἐτελείωσαν αὑτῶν τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἐν τῇ τοῦ Σωτῆρος ὁμολογίᾳ. Τινὲς δὲ τῶν πιστῶν, λαθραίως αὐτῶν τὰ σώματα λαβόντες κατέθεντο ἐν τόπῳ ἐπιτηδείῳ συνεργασάσης αὐτοῖς τῆς χάριτος τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Rusticus condemns the martyrs; they are beheaded and buried
orientation: Rusticus the prefect pronounces the death sentence on Justin and his companions, and the narrative then records their execution and secret burial by believers.
pass_a_gloss: Rusticus the prefect pronounced sentence, saying: 'Those who were not willing to sacrifice to the gods and to yield to the command of the emperor, having been scourged, let them be led away, paying the capital penalty according to the sequence of the laws.' The holy martyrs, glorifying God, having gone out to the customary place, were beheaded, and they completed their martyrdom in the confession of the Savior. And some of the faithful, having secretly taken their bodies, laid them in a suitable place, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ having worked together with them, to whom be the glory unto the ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the legal phrase; κεφαλικήν means 'capital' (pertaining to the head), and ἀποτιννύντες δίκην means 'paying the penalty'.

choices.english: according to the sequence of the laws
choices.why: ἀκολουθία means 'sequence' or 'following'; the phrase indicates the prescribed legal process.
rejected: according to the order of the laws

choices.why: συνήθη means 'customary' or 'usual'; the place of execution is not further specified.
τελειόω means 'to complete' or 'bring to fulfillment'; μαρτυρία is rendered 'martyrdom' per the glossary.

choices.english: the grace having worked together with them
choices.why: συνεργάζομαι means 'to work together with'; the genitive absolute construction is kept literal.

pass_b_english: The prefect Rusticus pronounced sentence: "Those who have refused to sacrifice to the gods and to yield to the emperor's command are to be scourged and led away to pay the capital penalty in accordance with the laws."
The holy martyrs glorified God, went out to the customary place, and were beheaded, and so they completed their martyrdom in the confession of the Savior.
Some of the faithful secretly took their bodies and laid them in a suitable place, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ assisting them. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.

problems.quote: according to the sequence of the laws
problems.why: 'Sequence of the laws' is odd English; likely means 'in accordance with the laws' or 'by due process.'
problems.fix: Render as 'in accordance with the laws' or 'by due legal process.'

variants.text: according to the sequence of the laws

edits.old: according to the sequence of the laws

fixed: Changed 'according to the sequence of the laws' to 'in accordance with the laws': the Greek κατὰ τὴν τῶν νόμων ἀκολουθίαν means 'according to the following of the laws,' i.e., in accordance with the laws or by due legal process; 'sequence of the laws' is a literalistic rendering that misstates the sense.

problems.quote: the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ working together with them
problems.why: 'Working together with them' applied to grace is odd; Greek synergei likely means 'cooperating' or 'assisting.'

edits.old: the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ working together with them
edits.new: the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ assisting them

fixed: Changed 'working together with them' to 'assisting them' for συνεργασάσης, since the grace is the agent helping the faithful, not a co-worker.
